subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw treat two same-turn Codex dynamic-tool requests with different `callId`s but equal payloads as one retryable operation, or as independent operations by default?
rationale: The implementation deliberately changes a call-ID-based execution boundary, while the provided evidence proves coalescing behavior but not the upstream semantic guarantee needed to suppress a separately correlated request.

options.title: Preserve distinct call IDs
options.body: Keep `callId` in the execution identity and pursue duplicate prevention only through an explicitly established retry signal or upstream contract.

options.title: Adopt payload coalescing
options.body: Accept cross-`callId` coalescing only after documenting the Codex contract and adding coverage that independent equal calls cannot be legitimate.

recommendation.title: Preserve distinct call IDs
recommendation.body: Keep `callId` in the execution identity and pursue duplicate prevention only through an explicitly established retry signal or upstream contract.

likelyOwner.reason: A verified current-main history pass is still needed to route the Codex runtime contract to a concrete owner.
